strategy.publicationPosture: Direct-gauge routes become score-eligible only when a recognized paddling or official manager source publishes a numeric range tied to the selected gauge and the same reach. Proxy-gauge and unguided stage routes remain planning-only.
strategy.thresholdPosture: Use published minimum and maximum values as hard shoulders. Where a source publishes one average rather than an ideal interval, derive a narrow, clearly labeled ideal band around that average and mark the source strength mixed. The Upper Lochsa White Pine-to-Wilderness Gateway card uses direct USGS 13337000 Lowell context, American Whitewater's Class IV endpoint chain, and Snoflo's 3,000-5,000 cfs recommendation; 2,000-8,000 cfs is retained as a conservative mixed-source envelope, with cold water, wood, incidents, and local scouting overriding the score. Spring Creek routes use the stricter IDFG 2,000 cfs access floor. The Main Payette combines BLM's 2,000-10,000 cfs ideal range with American Whitewater's 800-12,000 cfs runnable shoulders. The Lower Main Payette uses How's Your River's explicit 1,200-15,000 cfs runnable range, with a 2,000-10,000 cfs summer planning band and a warning that October's 800-1,200 cfs is runnable but low and technical. The Middle Fork Payette Nozzle section now uses American Whitewater's direct 13237920 gauge with a roughly 400 cfs practical floor and 800-1,500 cfs spring runoff window; no unsupported high-flow cutoff is presented, and wood/creek hydraulics override any numeric score. The upper North Fork Payette Rotary Park-to-Sheep Creek Bridge card uses the direct 13239000 McCall gauge, American Whitewater's 1,000-3,500 cfs ideal range, and the Idaho Payette Basin plan's 800 cfs minimum; no high-flow cutoff is invented, and current town-stretch wood alerts override the score. Downtown Boise uses How's Your River/American Whitewater's 1,500-3,000 cfs runnable range on the direct Glenwood Bridge gauge, with city guidance distinguishing the less-managed downstream corridor from the casual floater reach. The Boise urban route uses the official Float the Boise 500-1,500 cfs typical-season range. North Fork-to-Corn Creek Salmon now preserves How's Your River/American Whitewater's route-specific 600-8,000 cfs band on the direct Salmon-at-Salmon gauge, explicitly labeled a broad SWAG, with a conservative 1,500-4,000 cfs planning ideal and mandatory Corn Creek permit boundary. Carey Creek-to-Riggins preserves How's Your River/American Whitewater's 1,000-100,000 cfs White Bird gauge envelope, with a conservative 3,000-30,000 cfs operating band and high-flow expert hazard warning. The North Fork Clearwater, South Fork Clearwater, Bruneau, Jarbidge, Sunbeam, Hells Canyon, Pittsburg-Heller, Middle Fork Salmon, Lower Salmon, Priest River, North Fork Payette, and Middle Fork Boise cards preserve published paddling guidance as explicit two-sided shoulders. South Fork Boise Upper retains Kayak Idaho's 600-2,000 cfs planning band plus American Whitewater's higher-flow hazard report, and remains planning-only. North Fork Owyhee retains the BLM/American Whitewater 1,500-3,000 cfs spring window as a minimum-only planning cue because the Rome gauge is a downstream proxy. South Fork Payette Canyon now retains the Idaho Payette basin plan's 600-3,000 cfs window as a minimum-only planning cue, with American Whitewater's Class III-IV reach description and the Lowman gauge as proxy context. Staircase retains the Idaho Payette basin plan's 600-4,000 cfs window as a minimum-only planning cue, with American Whitewater's broader range as context, because the practical gauge is proxy context. Main Salmon preserves RiverBrain's 4,000-35,000 cfs envelope with a 20,000 cfs average and a 12,000-28,000 cfs planning ideal, but remains planning-only because the practical gauge is proxy context. Priest River uses the preferred 1,200-1,600 cfs band inside 900-4,500 cfs shoulders, North Fork Payette uses the RiverBrain 750-3,000 cfs envelope with a 1,500 cfs average reference, Jarbidge uses completionSummaryCurrent: Current authoritative summary: 125 Idaho routes across 55 river/lake groups, with 91 direct-gauge routes, 34 proxy-gauge routes, 70 score-eligible routes, and 55 planning-only routes. The latest additions include Upper Fall River Cave Falls Campground-to-Concrete CCC Bridge (14.7 miles, Class III-IV(V), direct 13047500, local 1,500 cfs minimum cue), Teton Dam Site-to-Teton Forks (6.9 miles, Class II-III, downstream proxy 13055000, repeated trip-report cue around 500 cfs), Ketchum Rotary Park-to-Broadway Run Road (4.9 miles, Class II, direct same-river 13135500 context with no route-specific numeric cutoff), Crooked Fork Highway 12 Bridge-to-White Sands Campground (7.2 miles, Class III, Lowell proxy 13337000, 5,500 cfs low-end and 8,000-15,000 cfs preferred-flow cues), Marsh Creek Highway 21-to-Dagger Falls (16 miles, Class III+, Middle Fork Lodge stage proxy 13309220, 2.5-3.5 ft preferred context with 4.5 ft high shoulder), Big Creek end-of-road/Middle Fork hike-in-to-bridge (9 miles, Class III-IV, Calder proxy 12414500, 5,000 cfs low-water cue), Smith Creek Bridge-to-Above Smith Creek Falls (5.7 miles, Class IV-V+, regional proxy 12321500, 100 cfs minimum / 200-300 cfs medium hydro-release cues), and St. Maries River Mashburn-to-St. Joe (28.1 miles, Class II-III, direct 12414900, 600-3,000 cfs runnable correlation and 1,000-2,000 cfs conservative planning band). Smith Creek remains planning-only because release volume is variable, the gauge is regional proxy context, and falls, wood, remote access, and expert rescue controls require current verification; St. Maries remains planning-only because AW access coordinates are approximate and the reach is long, committed, and wood-sensitive. Teton Dam remains planning-only because the 500 cfs cue is trip-report-derived and the launch requires a gated-road carry; Big Wood Rotary remains planning-only because AW gives only a seasonal window and warns of river-wide log jams; Crooked Fork remains planning-only because its threshold is proxy/mixed and its bridge and campground endpoints require current carry/landing confirmation; Marsh Creek remains planning-only because its stage gauge is downstream proxy context and 2026 wood conditions require current scouting; Big Creek remains planning-only because its threshold is a downstream proxy and the remote hike-in, wood, bridge, and road-access controls require current verification. Existing Big Wood, Boise, Lower Deadwood, Upper Selway, Little North Fork, Lochsa, Kelly Creek, Hidden Creek, East Fork South Fork Salmon, and Owyhee threshold cards remain documented in the evidence ledger.
